idea: Find the groups of nodes in a directed graph that can all reach each other. One depth-first search gives every node an index and a low-link, the smallest index it can reach through the search and one back edge to a node still on the stack. When a node's low-link equals its own index, it is the root of a group, and everything above it on the stack belongs to that group.
useWhen: Finding mutually dependent modules or cyclic dependencies
Shrinking a directed graph to a graph of groups with no cycles
Solving problems where every cycle must be treated as one unit
avoidWhen: The graph is undirected: use plain connected components instead
You only need to know whether any cycle exists: a simple search is enough
